name: MKOBJ
desc: Covers the MKOBJ expression in its alternating name/value, parallel name/value array, and property-pair array forms. Tests require string names, uniqueness, correct shapes and lengths, value-context evaluation, arbitrary property names, independent constructed values, scopes, nested expressions, SPLIT metadata carried by array values, pending deletions, and error propagation. Shape and name errors described by MKOBJ are INVALID_TARGET.

tests.name: Alternating names and values
tests.desc: One or more name/value pairs construct own properties. Values may be any JSON type and expressions are evaluated in the caller scope. No name coercion is performed.

tests.name: Parallel arrays
tests.desc: Exactly two array-valued operands select parallel arrays. Their lengths must match; empty arrays construct an empty object. Each value stays one property value without flattening.

tests.name: Property-pair arrays
tests.desc: Exactly one array-valued operand holds two-element arrays. Both empty and populated lists are supported. Pair positions are strict and names remain strings.

tests.name: Input list is borrowed only for evaluation
Pair list constructor evaluates names and values
Nested CONCAT assembles a property list
Names and uniqueness
tests.desc: Names are compared as exact strings with no Unicode normalization or numeric coercion. Empty strings, numeric spellings, inherited method names, controls, and arbitrary keys become ordinary own properties. Duplicate names are rejected in every form.

tests.name: Invalid names and shapes
tests.desc: MKOBJ shape errors, including absent pairs, incomplete pairs, mismatched arrays, non-array property lists, and pair lengths other than two, produce INVALID_TARGET. Expression syntax errors retain INVALID_GRAFT.

tests.name: Flat list is not a list of pairs
Additional arrays do not select parallel form
Second argument array does not coerce the first name
Scopes, independence, and value semantics
tests.desc: Names and values use the original caller current node. CONST, STASH, TEMP, common expressions, and matching contexts retain their ordinary value semantics. Result edits cannot modify referenced source data.

tests.name: IS compares a complete constructed object
Parsed dates retain virtual fields in stash
Pending deletion in values is invalid
Subsequent COPY pairs can read the result
Computed key does not rebind the value current node
Failure propagation and limits
tests.desc: Missing values, invalid nested expressions, and explicit FAIL propagate without publishing a partially constructed object. Match probes trap INVALID_TARGET while RESOURCE_LIMIT and unsupported-host failures remain fatal.
